stem.en: The eggs of fish, frogs and insects carry only a small amount of yolk. What does this mean for the young one?

text.en: It hatches as a larva that feeds

feedback.en: Yes. The yolk lasts only until a feeding stage hatches.

text.en: It never hatches from the egg

feedback.en: These eggs do hatch. The yolk is enough to produce a larva.

text.en: It hatches looking like the adult

feedback.en: That fits birds and reptiles, whose eggs have more yolk.

text.en: It stays and grows inside the mother's body

feedback.en: Fish, frogs and insects lay their eggs outside the body.

explanation.en: Yolk is the food stored in an egg. A small amount is just enough to produce a larva, which then feeds before it becomes an adult.

hints.en: What is a caterpillar doing most of the time?
